title: LICM — hoisting loop invariants
summary_caption: LICM = fixpoint marking (x, then t1 by propagation) + dominator-order hoisting into the preheader.

nodes.label:
for.body
x = y + z
t1 = x * x
a[i] = 6*i + t1

frames.caption: The note's LICM example, in LoopSimplify form: the empty preheader is where hoisted code will go.
Scan the body top-down (dominator order), so defs are seen before uses. First candidate: x = y + z.
y and z are never defined inside the loop, so every operand is invariant: mark x = y + z.

set_labels.body:
for.body
x = y + z [inv]
t1 = x * x
a[i] = 6*i + t1

frames.caption: t1 = x * x: operand x IS defined in the loop, but that single def is itself marked invariant. Mark t1.

set_labels.body:
for.body
x = y + z [inv]
t1 = x * x [inv]
a[i] = 6*i + t1

frames.caption: a[i] = 6*i + t1 and i = i + 1 depend on i, which changes every iteration. Fixpoint reached: two invariants.
Legality: defs are unique and dominate their uses; both are pure arithmetic, so even a zero-trip loop is unharmed.
Hoist in dominator order: x = y + z moves to the preheader and now runs once, before the loop.

set_labels.body:
for.body
t1 = x * x [inv]
a[i] = 6*i + t1

frames.caption: t1 = x * x follows. Hoisting it first would break dominance: its operand x had to move up first.

set_labels.pre:
preheader
x = y + z
t1 = x * x

frames.caption: The body now does only a[i] = 6*i + t1: the invariant work runs once instead of n times.
